Looking for a Function

03 / THREE SIMPLE STEPS
STEP 01

Loss Function

Decide what “good” actually means by defining an error score to minimize.

STEP 02

Pick a Model

Set a family of candidate functions—from linear weights to deep neural nets.

STEP 03

Gradient Descent

Take guided steps downhill to steadily find the best-performing parameters.

“Cartoons instead of dry formulas. Pretty simple, right?”

FIG. 04 — BASIC ML FRAMEWORK Prof. Lee’s 3-step visual roadmap for machine learning
Arrows / Space / 1-9 to navigate 04 / 09

Reading a Loss Curve

04 / DIAGNOSTICS & ITERATION
FIG. 05 — TRAINING LOSS CURVE When you train a model, the curve guides every adjustment
SIGNAL 1

Line Goes Down

When you train a model, if the curve trends smoothly downward, the computer is genuinely learning.

SIGNAL 2

Stuck & Flat

If the curve flattens out early, something is off—tweak hyperparameters and try again.

MINDSET

Iterate Step by Step

You’ll definitely make mistakes at first—just do your best and fix them one run at a time.
